title: Stuck in Maintenance Mode
description: Remove maintenance mode after failed updates — .maintenance file, plugin lockouts, or hosting maintenance pages.

steps.title: Identify Maintenance Source
steps.instructions: Determine if the message is WordPress core ('Briefly unavailable'), a maintenance plugin, or host-level maintenance page.

steps.title: Delete .maintenance File
steps.instructions: Remove .maintenance from the WordPress root via SFTP. This file is created during core/plugin/theme updates and should auto-delete — stale files cause stuck maintenance.

steps.title: Complete or Roll Back Failed Update
steps.instructions: Check if a partial update left mixed file versions. Re-run the update or restore wp-admin/wp-includes from a matching WordPress zip.

steps.title: Disable Maintenance Plugins
steps.instructions: Deactivate WP Maintenance Mode, SeedProd, or similar via SFTP if admin is inaccessible. Remove maintenance.php drop-ins in wp-content if present.

steps.title: Check Hosting Maintenance Toggle
steps.instructions: Some hosts have a one-click maintenance mode in the control panel. Disable it if you did not intentionally enable it.

steps.title: Verify Public Site Access
steps.instructions: Load the site from incognito and external monitoring. Confirm no maintenance message and admin is reachable.
